title: The size transports preserve identity and composition of field inclusions.
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, put $K=\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], and let $\Omega$ be a fixed algebraic closure of $K$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure], with its specified $K$-algebra structure. Let $I$ be the set of finite-dimensional intermediate fields $K\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$, ordered by inclusion [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. Fix a universe $u$. For each $E\in I$, write $C_E=\operatorname{Shrink}^{u}(E)$ for its canonical small copy with the field and $K$-algebra structures transported from $E$, and write $s_E:C_E\xrightarrow{\sim}_K E$ for the canonical algebra equivalence (Mathlib's $\operatorname{Shrink.algEquiv}$). Here the smallness witness is the one furnished by the finite-basis coordinate bijection $E\simeq K^{[E:K]}$, as in the coefficientSmall construction; no equality between the universes of $\Omega$ and $C_E$ is required. For $h:E\subseteq L$ let $\iota_h:E\to L$ be the inclusion, $x\mapsto x$ with its membership proof in $L$, and define the transported algebra homomorphism
$$j_h=s_L^{-1}\circ\iota_h\circ s_E:C_E\longrightarrow C_L.$$
Then both laws hold:
$$\forall E\in I,\quad j_{E\subseteq E}=\operatorname{id}_{C_E},$$
$$\forall E,L,M\in I,\ \forall h:E\subseteq L,\ \forall k:L\subseteq M,\quad j_k\circ j_h=j_{h\,\mathrm{trans}\,k}.$$
These are equalities of $K$-algebra homomorphisms for the actual canonical size transports.

proof.text: Fix $E\in I$ and $x\in C_E$. The self-inclusion sends the element $s_E(x)$ to itself, so $j_{E\subseteq E}(x)=s_E^{-1}(s_E(x))=x$ by the inverse identity for the algebra equivalence $s_E$. Equality on every element gives equality of the algebra homomorphisms (their remaining fields are proofs). This proves the first universal clause.

proof.text: Fix $E\subseteq L\subseteq M$, witnesses $h,k$, and $x\in C_E$. Expanding the definition gives $(j_k\circ j_h)(x)=s_M^{-1}(\iota_k(s_L(s_L^{-1}(\iota_h(s_E(x))))))=s_M^{-1}(\iota_k(\iota_h(s_E(x))))$. The middle cancellation is the inverse identity for $s_L$. Each inclusion keeps the same underlying element of $\Omega$; hence $\iota_k(\iota_h(s_E(x)))=\iota_{h\,\mathrm{trans}\,k}(s_E(x))$ as elements of $M$: the underlying values agree and membership proofs are irrelevant. The last expression is $j_{h\,\mathrm{trans}\,k}(x)$. Equality on every $x$ gives the second equality of algebra homomorphisms. The choices of $E,L,M,h,k$ were arbitrary, and conjunction introduction joins the two clauses.
